# AllClear — Product Requirements Document

**Version:** 1.0
**Date:** September 11, 2026
**Author:** Generated by Claude
**Status:** Draft

---

## 1. Overview

### 1.1 Problem Statement
People who want situational awareness about the places they care about — weather, wildfire, earthquakes, air quality, official emergency alerts — currently juggle four or five separate apps to get it: a weather app, a fire-tracking app, an air-quality app, USGS's own site for quakes, and whatever their county uses for alerts. Each has its own saved-locations list and its own notification settings, so the user re-enters the same city over and over. And every one of these apps is built for a single audience — a light user who just wants tomorrow's forecast gets the same interface as a scanner-obsessed prepper, because there's no way to say "I only care about weather and fire, hide the rest."

### 1.2 Proposed Solution
AllClear is a single dashboard where a user builds a personal "Watch List" of locations (home, a parent's city, an upcoming trip), and for each location picks which hazard layers matter to them — weather, wildfire, earthquakes, air quality, and official alerts. Every layer is sourced from a named, labeled public data feed (NWS, NASA FIRMS, USGS, AirNow), so the user always knows where a fact came from. The product is deliberately narrow for v1: no scanner audio, no AI-generated summaries, no social features — just a fast, trustworthy, radically simplified version of what five apps already do separately.

### 1.3 Goals
- **Primary goal:** A user can see a trustworthy, at-a-glance status for every place they care about, across every hazard type they choose to track, from one screen — replacing the need to check multiple apps.
- **Secondary goals:**
  - Build trust through transparent sourcing (every card names its data origin)
  - Ship on entirely free, official public APIs for MVP so the product has near-zero data-cost floor
  - Architect the backend API-first so a native mobile app (Phase 2) doesn't require a backend rewrite

### 1.4 Non-Goals (MVP)
- No police/fire scanner audio or CAD-partnership incident feed (Phase 4 in the original concept doc — a fundamentally different build with real licensing/partnership costs)
- No AI-generated "risk synthesis" card combining hazards into one summary — explicitly deferred to a later phase
- No native iOS/Android app — MVP targets web first, mobile is the confirmed next phase
- No global/non-US weather coverage — NWS is US-only; international coverage requires a paid commercial weather API and is out of scope for MVP
- No user-generated content: no photo submissions, comments, reactions, or social features
- No billing/subscription implementation — the freemium model is designed for, not built, in MVP

## 2. Target Users

### 2.1 Primary User Persona
| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Who | "The Weather & Wildfire Watcher" — e.g., a retiree or homeowner in a fire-exposed region |
| Pain | Checks 2-3 separate apps daily (weather app + a fire-tracking app) and re-enters the same cities in each |
| Goal | See tomorrow's forecast, the forecast for family in other cities, and how close active wildfires are to home — all in one place |
| Context | Checks first thing in the morning and again in the evening; during fire season, checks multiple times a day |
| Tech savvy | Low to medium — needs a simple, uncluttered interface, not a power-user dashboard |

### 2.2 Secondary Personas
- **The Everyday Safety Checker** — wants a quick "what's happening near me" without downloading a dedicated crime/incident app. Under-served by MVP (no incident layer yet) but served by the Official Alerts layer.
- **The Multi-City Tracker** — splits attention across several places (out-of-town family, an upcoming trip). Needs the Watch List to support unlimited locations, each independently configured, which MVP supports fully.

---

## 3. User Stories & Requirements

### 3.1 Watch Locations
**User story:** As a user, I want to save multiple locations and label them, so that I don't have to re-enter the same city every time I check a different hazard type.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] User can add a location by searching an address/city or dropping a pin on a map
- [ ] User can label a location (e.g., "Home," "Mom's house")
- [ ] User can mark one location as primary/default
- [ ] User can remove a saved location
- [ ] Unauthenticated users can view the national map but cannot save locations

### 3.2 Weather
**User story:** As a user, I want to see current conditions and the forecast for each of my saved locations, so that I know what to expect today, tomorrow, and at other places I care about.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Current temperature, conditions, and hourly forecast shown per saved location
- [ ] 7-day forecast available per saved location
- [ ] Active NWS severe weather alerts (e.g., Red Flag Warning) shown inline
- [ ] Multiple saved locations can be viewed side by side for comparison

### 3.3 Wildfire & Smoke
**User story:** As a user, I want to know about active wildfires near any of my saved locations, so that I can gauge risk without hunting through a separate fire-tracking app.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Map shows NASA FIRMS satellite hotspot detections and named InciWeb/NIFC incidents within a configurable radius of each saved location
- [ ] Each fire shows distance from the saved location, and (when available) containment %, acreage, and evacuation status
- [ ] User can enable/disable this layer per saved location independently

### 3.4 Earthquakes
**User story:** As a user, I want to be notified about earthquakes above a magnitude I choose near any of my saved locations, so that I don't have to check USGS manually.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Recent earthquakes (USGS feed) shown within a configurable radius of each saved location
- [ ] User can set a minimum magnitude threshold per location for this layer to surface/notify

### 3.5 Air Quality
**User story:** As a user, I want to see the current AQI at my saved locations, so that I know when smoke or pollution makes it unsafe to be outside.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Current AQI (AirNow) shown per saved location with the standard color-coded category
- [ ] User can set an AQI threshold per location above which they're notified

### 3.6 Official Alerts
**User story:** As a user, I want official government alerts for my saved locations surfaced automatically, so that I don't miss something my other layers don't cover.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] Active NWS/CAP-formatted alerts shown per saved location, always on (not a togglable layer — this is the safety net)
- [ ] Alert severity (Advisory/Watch/Warning) is visually distinct

### 3.7 Notifications
**User story:** As a user, I want to set my own thresholds for when I get notified, so that I'm not spammed with every minor update.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- [ ] User can set per-location, per-layer notification rules (distance threshold for fires, magnitude threshold for quakes, AQI threshold, on/off for official alerts)
- [ ] Notifications delivered via web push and email
- [ ] User has an in-app history of past notifications sent

## 4. Feature List

### MVP (Must-Have)
| # | Feature | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Account creation & login | P0 | Supabase Auth, email/password |
| 2 | Watch Locations (add/label/remove, unlimited) | P0 | Core personalization primitive |
| 3 | Per-location layer toggles | P0 | Weather / Wildfire / Earthquakes / AQI; Official Alerts always on |
| 4 | Weather module (current + hourly + 7-day + NWS alerts) | P0 | NWS API |
| 5 | Wildfire & Smoke module (FIRMS + InciWeb, proximity) | P0 | See Tech Spec §5 for InciWeb access assumption |
| 6 | Earthquake module (USGS, proximity + magnitude filter) | P0 | USGS API |
| 7 | Air Quality module (AirNow, per location) | P0 | AirNow API |
| 8 | Official Alerts module | P0 | NWS active alerts endpoint (see Tech Spec §5 re: IPAWS) |
| 9 | Notification rules (thresholds) + web push + email delivery | P0 | |
| 10 | National public map (fires, quakes) — no login required | P1 | Top-of-funnel / shareable |
| 11 | Notification history | P1 | |

### Phase 2 (Nice-to-Have)
| # | Feature | Priority | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Native iOS/Android app | P1 | Confirmed next phase after web validates |
| 2 | Global/international weather coverage | P2 | Requires a paid commercial weather API |
| 3 | AI-generated cross-hazard "risk synthesis" card | P2 | Explicitly deferred from MVP |
| 4 | Flooding/river gauge module | P2 | |
| 5 | Native push notifications | P1 | Ships with native app |

### Out of Scope
| Feature | Reason |
|---|---|
| Police/fire scanner audio or CAD partnership feed | Requires either per-jurisdiction partnerships or a licensed third-party feed — a fundamentally different scope of build than the rest of the product |
| Social features (comments, reactions, user photo/video submissions) | Adds moderation burden without validating the core value prop first |
| Subscription billing | Freemium model is designed for structurally but not implemented until there's a paid tier worth charging for |

## 5. Success Metrics

| Metric | Target | How Measured |
|---|---|---|
| Activation: % of signups who add ≥1 Watch Location in first session | 60%+ | Event tracking on location creation vs. signup |
| Engagement: weekly active users returning to the dashboard | 40%+ of registered users | Session logs |
| Retention: % of users still active at day 30 | 25%+ | Cohort retention analysis |
| Depth of use: average Watch Locations per active user | 2+ | DB query |

---

## 6. Assumptions & Risks

| # | Assumption / Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | InciWeb has no confirmed clean public JSON API | Medium | Poller falls back to NIFC's public open-data/ArcGIS feeds or InciWeb's RSS feed; verify exact endpoint during implementation (see Tech Spec §5) |
| 2 | IPAWS itself isn't a general-purpose consumer API (it's built for certified alerting authorities to originate alerts, not for third parties to subscribe to) | Medium | MVP treats NWS's own active-alerts endpoint as the practical stand-in for "official alerts"; revisit if broader all-hazards coverage is needed |
| 3 | Free government APIs can rate-limit, go down, or change schema without notice, and AllClear has no support contract with any of them | High | Cache-first architecture (see Tech Spec) so a single source outage degrades one layer, not the whole product; graceful per-source failure handling |
| 4 | Wrong or late emergency information carries real liability | High | Facts-only presentation, explicit source labeling on every card, no editorializing or prediction — modeled directly on how Watch Duty positions itself |
| 5 | "Weather in other places" is a core ask (per original request) but MVP is US-only | Medium | Explicitly scoped as a Non-Goal for MVP; flagged as the first Phase 2 priority |

---

## 7. Open Questions

- [ ] Do we pursue a CAD/PulsePoint-style formal partnership for public safety incidents eventually, or license an existing feed (e.g., from Citizen or a Broadcastify-style aggregator)? This is a Phase 4 decision, not urgent, but affects whether we should design the data model to accommodate it now.
- [ ] Which framework for the Phase 2 native app — React Native/Expo (code-sharing with the Next.js web app) or fully separate native builds?
- [ ] Does the safety-adjacent nature of this product require legal review of the Privacy Policy/Terms of Service before public launch, beyond the standard boilerplate?
